title: South-east Australian runoff lows of 1959-1971 and 1983-1995 kept the 1951-1996 rain sensitivity, but the same catchments lost 22-31% of it after 1997 (175 CAMELS-AUS catchments, annual rain models)
abstract: Earlier campaign work found that the post-1997 runoff deficit in south-east Australia equals the 1959-1971 and 1983-1995 lows in size. We asked if it is the same process. We used 175 CAMELS-AUS catchments (1951-2021) and 34 long Bureau of Meteorology records (1912-2022), with per-catchment annual rain models fitted on 1951-1996 without the tested window. Planned test 1: across catchments, the earlier departures and the 2010-2021 departure had rank correlations of +0.34 (1959-1971) and +0.14 (1983-1995). A stationary block-permutation null gave +0.26 (5-95%: -0.23 to +0.69), because one shared calibration error enters both departures. Thus the pattern test could not show recurrence. Planned test 3: the earlier lows were nearly parallel shifts; the change of the rain slope was -0.04 and -0.05 (inside the null). In the same catchments, the rain slope fell by 22-31% in 2010-2021 (null p <= 0.02) with AGCD or SILO rain, a temperature term or a quadratic rain term. The NSW 1983-1995 low was as deep as the post-1997 deficit but kept its slope. Post hoc, long records show two stages: rain slopes were 1.2-1.3 times the 1957-1996 slope in 1937-1966, and 0.75-0.86 times it in 2010-2022 at near-normal rain. Planned test 2: the loss of cool-season rain explains 12% (3-18%) of the 2010-2021 deficit and does not match where it occurred (Spearman +0.02). Limitations: low power of the pattern test, linear annual models, few gauges before 1957, and no land-use or rating tests.

citations.reason: We reuse its annual CAMELS-AUS flow, rain and temperature tables and 175-catchment set; our results support its post-1997 rain-slope loss and show that the earlier low windows did not have it.
It found that post-1997 group departures equal the 1959-1971 and 1983-1995 lows; we find that these lows differ in form (no rain-slope loss in the 1951-1996 frame).
We reuse its BoM flow scripts and test its cool-season rain result at the catchment scale (12% here against its 32%).
